title: Dynamic intake scoring and eligibility pipeline for hosted multi-output requests (chat, streaming, tool calls, structured outputs)
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: Enterprise customers submit hosted API feature requests that mix requirements across chat, streaming, tool/function calling, and structured outputs. Current intake is manual-heavy, inconsistent across account managers, and frequently mis-prioritizes work that has predictable cost or regulatory implications. We need an automated, explainable scoring and eligibility pipeline that standardizes incoming requests, surfaces high-risk/regulatory needs, and outputs a recommended routing (self-serve backlog, PM review, sales-assisted enterprise path, or SLA/engineering fast-track).
goals: Create a deterministic scoring model combining product signals (request type, expected QPS, streaming vs non-streaming, tool-call surface area), commercial signals (customer tier, ARR, committed capacity), and technical risk (data residency, structured output schema complexity)
Expose transparent eligibility gates and recommended routing actions (self-serve docs, sandbox pilot, Dedicated/Dedicated+Private presales)
Provide clear explainability flags for reviewers: top contributing signals and a one-line rationale
Reduce PM triage time by 40% and increase high-value enterprise routing recall by 25% within Q2 rollout
acceptance_criteria: Intake form prototype collects required signals for chat, streaming, tool calls, and structured outputs (schema attachments or example payloads)
Automated scoring engine runs on new requests and returns: numeric score 0-100, primary routing recommendation, top 3 score contributors, and a risk category
Routing recommendations map to existing lanes: Self-Serve, PM Review, Sales-Assisted, Dedicated Evaluation, Private/VPC Presales
Dashboard card available in Console intake view for PMs with filtering by score range and by feature type
End-to-end tests for scoring reproducibility and guardrails for requests flagged as 'high regulatory risk'
out_of_scope: Automatically approving Dedicated or Private deployments (this ticket only recommends routing)
Replacing contract negotiation or SOC/compliance review workflows
Building a full ML model for scoring; initial rollout should be rule-based with telemetry hooks
constraints: Must not require customers to submit sensitive PII via intake form (only metadata and example payloads)
Scoring must be explainable (no black-box in first two releases)
Integrations with Console UI need to follow current RBAC patterns
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce a rule-based scoring engine that ingests intake fields and synthesized signals (customer tier from CRM, recent API usage, estimated QPS) to compute a score and routing recommendation. Provide a short textual rationale per request and surface a 'why' panel for reviewers. Implement as a serverless scoring microservice behind the existing intake API; store outputs as metadata on the Linear ticket and in a Console dataset for visualization.
signal_definitions: EstimatedQPS: integer estimate from customer or derived from usage data
CustomerTier: Free | Developer | Startup | Midmarket | Enterprise
ComplianceFlag: none | GDPR-only | GDPR+PCI | FedRAMP required
SchemaComplexity: simple (single object) | medium (nested arrays) | complex (multi-entity relations)
ToolCallSurface: number of external integrations + expected concurrency
routing_matrix_high_level: Score 0-30 => Self-Serve backlog (provide best-practice templates + docs)
Score 56-80 => Sales-Assisted / Dedicated Evaluation (engage solutions team)
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Rule-based first: faster rollout and explainability vs delayed accuracy compared to supervised ML
Use CRM-derived commercial signals: better routing for revenue-generating customers but requires syncing cadence and privacy checks
Expose scoring and rationale to customers in a limited form to reduce confusion; initially only show routing suggestion in support responses
Keep high regulatory flags conservative to avoid leakage; flagging may cause more manual review but reduces compliance risk
implementation_plan: Week 1: Finalize intake form fields and telemetry contract with SDK/UI team
Week 2: Implement rule engine prototype and unit tests; build mock scoring API
Week 3: Integrate with Console intake view + add reviewer panel showing rationale
Week 4: Pilot with 3 customer success reps and 2 enterprise accounts; collect feedback
Week 5: Iterate rules, add analytics, and enable wide rollout behind feature flag
metrics: Correct routing precision for enterprise requests (manual review baseline) - target +25% recall
Percent of flagged high-regulatory requests later escalated to compliance - target >95% precision
False positive rate for fast-track routing - target <5%
risks: Overfitting rules to early pilot customers resulting in poor generalization
Operational burden on CS if many medium-scoring items require manual review
Misclassification could cause SLA commitments to be promised prematurely
